title: Direct image of etale sheaves of modules over a constant ring: module structure, additive and left exact
statement: Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $R$ a commutative ring. For a scheme $T$ let $T_{\Et}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ the category of abelian sheaves on it [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $R_T$ the constant sheaf of rings with value $R$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a sheaf $G$ of abelian groups or of commutative rings on $U_{\Et}$ let $u_*G$ be the sheaf $W\mapsto G(W\times_VU)$ on $V_{\Et}$, $W\times_VU$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], with restriction along $g:W_1\to W_2$ that of $G$ along $g\times\mathrm{id}_U$ (a sheaf of the same kind by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]). Let $\rho:R_V\to u_*R_U$ be the morphism of sheaves of rings which, by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], extends the morphism from the constant presheaf of rings with value $R$ on $V_{\Et}$ to $u_*R_U$ whose component at $W$ is the map $R\to R_U(W\times_VU)$ of the sheafification morphism of the constant presheaf $R$ on $U_{\Et}$. Then: (1) for $F\in\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$ the abelian sheaf $u_*F$, with the action $R_V(W)\times F(W\times_VU)\to F(W\times_VU)$, $(a,s)\mapsto\rho_W(a)\,s$, is a sheaf of $R_V$-modules, and for an $R_U$-linear morphism $\varphi:F\to F'$ the morphism $u_*\varphi$, $(u_*\varphi)_W=\varphi_{W\times_VU}$, is $R_V$-linear; this defines a functor $u_*:\Mod(U_{\Et},R)\to\Mod(V_{\Et},R)$ whose composite with the forgetful functor to $\Ab(V_{\Et})$ is the composite of the forgetful functor to $\Ab(U_{\Et})$ with $u_*:\Ab(U_{\Et})\to\Ab(V_{\Et})$; (2) this functor is additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]: it preserves finite products and kernels, so for every exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3$ of $\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$ the sequence $0\to u_*F_1\to u_*F_2\to u_*F_3$ is exact in $\Mod(V_{\Et},R)$.
